description: Experience the ultimate comfort food with our Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani recipe. This iconic Indian dish features tender chicken pieces simmered in a rich, creamy tomato-based sauce, subtly spiced and utterly irresistible. Perfect for a hearty lunch, it promises a delightful culinary journey to India.

ingredients.item: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast

ingredients.notes: soaked in warm water for 15 minutes

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger garlic paste, lemon juice, Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, and salt. Mix well to coat the chicken evenly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours for best results.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until browned and slightly charred. Remove chicken and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon ginger garlic paste, cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Saute for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Sauce
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato puree or crushed tomatoes. Add the soaked cashews (drained) and sugar. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the tomatoes to break down. Stir occasionally.

instructions.title: Blend and Strain the Sauce
instructions.text: Carefully remove the bay leaf, cinnamon stick, and cardamom pods (if you can find them). Transfer the sauce mixture to a blender and blend until completely smooth. For an extra silky sauce, pass it through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan. This step is crucial for authentic Murgh Makhani texture.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Return the cooked chicken to the smooth sauce. Stir in the crushed Kasoori Methi. Add the heavy cream and the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter. Simmer gently for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to warm through and absorb the sauce flavors. Do not boil after adding cream.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Taste and adjust salt or sugar if needed. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve hot with naan bread, roti, or basmati rice. Enjoy your homemade Butter Chicken!

tips: For a deeper color and flavor, use Kashmiri red chili powder which is milder but provides a vibrant red hue. If unavailable, use a mix of regular chili powder and paprika.
Soaking cashews is key for a truly creamy and smooth sauce without adding too much heavy cream. Do not skip blending the sauce until absolutely smooth.
Always add cream and the final knob of butter at the very end and do not boil the sauce vigorously afterward to prevent the cream from splitting and to retain its rich texture.
article:
Unlock the secrets to making the most beloved Indian dish right in your own kitchen! Butter Chicken, known in India as Murgh Makhani, is a culinary masterpiece that has captivated palates worldwide with its rich, creamy texture and subtly spiced tomato gravy. Perfect for a comforting Indian lunch, this dish offers a delightful balance of sweet, tangy, and savory flavors that are simply irresistible. If you've ever dreamt of recreating that authentic restaurant-style Murgh Makhani, you're in the right place. This comprehensive guide will walk you through every step, ensuring your homemade version is nothing short of spectacular.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, translates literally to "chicken with butter" and is a classic Indian curry originating from Delhi in the 1950s. It’s a dish celebrated for its tender pieces of chicken, traditionally cooked in a tandoor (clay oven) or pan-fried, swimming in a luxurious, vibrant orange-red sauce. The sauce is the star, a velvety blend of pureed tomatoes, ginger, garlic, and a medley of aromatic spices like garam masala, cumin, and fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi). What gives it its signature richness and smoothness is the generous addition of butter and cream, which mellow out the spices and create an incredibly comforting and satisfying experience. Unlike many other Indian curries, Murgh Makhani is typically mild, making it a fantastic entry point for those new to Indian cuisine, while still offering complex layers of flavor for seasoned enthusiasts. It’s a quintessential Indian lunch recipe that promises warmth and indulgence.

## Ingredients You Need for Butter Chicken

Crafting the perfect Butter Chicken requires a few key components, divided into the chicken marinade and the luscious sauce. Fresh, quality ingredients are paramount for the best flavor.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   1.5 lbs boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 tsp red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color)
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1/2 tsp garam masala
*   Salt to taste

For the Murgh Makhani Sauce:
*   2 tbsp unsalted butter
*   1 tbsp oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 can (28 oz) crushed tomatoes or 4-5 ripe fresh tomatoes, pureed
*   1/2 cup cashews, soaked in warm water for 15 minutes (optional, for extra creaminess)
*   1 tsp red chili powder
*   1 tsp garam masala
*   1 tsp ground cumin
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1 tsp kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1/4 cup heavy cream
*   1 tbsp sugar or honey (to balance acidity)
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Murgh Makhani

Follow these steps carefully to create a magnificent Butter Chicken that will impress even the most discerning palates.

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all marinade ingredients. Mix well to ensure the chicken is evenly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, to allow the flavors to penetrate.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if necessary. Sear until browned and slightly charred on all sides, and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove the cooked chicken and set aside.
3.  **Prepare the Sauce Base:** In the same pan, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté until translucent and lightly golden, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.
4.  **Add Tomatoes and Spices:** Pour in the crushed tomatoes (or fresh tomato puree). If using, add the soaked and drained cashews now. Stir in the red chili powder, garam masala, ground cumin, and turmeric powder. Mix well and bring the mixture to a simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 10-15 minutes, allowing the tomatoes to break down and the sauce to thicken slightly.
5.  **Blend the Sauce:** Carefully transfer the cooked sauce mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. For an extra silky sauce, you can pass it through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan.
6.  **Finish the Sauce:** Return the smooth sauce to the pan over low-medium heat. Stir in the kasoori methi, sugar (or honey), and salt to taste. Add the cooked chicken pieces to the sauce.
7.  **Add Cream and Serve:** Gently stir in the heavy cream. Simmer for another 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to absorb the sauce. Do not boil vigorously after adding cream. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro. Your homemade Butter Chicken is ready!

## Pro Tips for the Best Butter Chicken

Achieving that restaurant-quality Murgh Makhani at home is entirely possible with a few expert tricks:

*   **Marination is Key:** The longer you marinate the chicken, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight marination truly makes a difference.
*   **Char the Chicken:** Don't just cook the chicken; get some good browning and slight char on it. This adds a smoky depth of flavor that mimics the tandoor and is crucial for authentic Butter Chicken. If you have a grill or broiler, a quick finish under intense heat can elevate this.
*   **Blend Until Silky Smooth:** A powerful blender is your friend here. Blend the sauce thoroughly until there are no visible chunks. For the ultimate smoothness, pass it through a fine-mesh sieve. This step is non-negotiable for that classic Murgh Makhani texture.
*   **Don't Skip the Kasoori Methi:** Dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) are a signature ingredient in Butter Chicken. Crush them between your palms before adding to release their aromatic, slightly bitter, and sweet notes.
*   **Balance Flavors:** Taste your sauce! Tomatoes can be quite acidic, so don't be afraid to adjust with a little sugar or honey to balance it out. Similarly, add salt gradually.
*   **Fresh Ingredients:** Whenever possible, use fresh ginger and garlic, crushed into a paste, rather than pre-made jars for superior flavor.

## Serving Suggestions for Murgh Makhani

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with a variety of accompaniments, making it a truly satisfying Indian lunch.

*   **Naan Bread:** The classic pairing! Warm, fluffy naan is perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich sauce. Garlic naan or butter naan are particularly delightful.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a lovely contrast and helps soak up the luxurious gravy.
*   **Raita:** A cooling yogurt-based side dish, such as cucumber raita, offers a refreshing counterpoint to the richness of the curry.
*   **Salad:** A simple side salad with thinly sliced red onions, cucumber, and tomatoes can add freshness.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is perfect, feel free to experiment:

*   **Vegetarian Murgh Makhani:** Substitute chicken with paneer (Indian cheese), tofu, or mixed vegetables like cauliflower and potatoes. Add them in the last 10 minutes of cooking the sauce to absorb the flavors.
*   **Spicier Version:** Increase the amount of red chili powder or add a finely chopped green chili to the sauce base if you prefer more heat.
*   **Lighter Version:** Reduce the amount of cream or substitute with a lighter milk alternative, though this will slightly alter the richness. You can also use a bit more yogurt in the marinade and less butter in the sauce.
*   **Nut-Free:** If you have a nut allergy, you can omit the cashews. The sauce will still be delicious, perhaps slightly less thick, but equally flavorful. You can use a tablespoon of gram flour (besan) roasted in the pan for thickening instead.

Embrace the joy of cooking this iconic Murgh Makhani at home. With this guide, you’re not just making a meal; you’re creating an experience. Enjoy your delicious homemade Butter Chicken!
